summary: Stepper motor controller on a rectangular PCB. It has a USB micro-B connector on the top edge, a header-pin row along the left edge, and a 6-position screw terminal block along the right edge. A tall electrolytic capacitor and several small surface-mount parts sit on the top face. Two mounting holes are visible at opposite corners.

mountingSurfaces.description: Underside of the PCB, a flat face with only small surface-mount parts. It is the likely seating face for standoffs through the two corner holes.

notes: X and Y come from the printed dimensions in the photo (1.5 in x 1.05 in, i.e. 38.1 x 26.67 mm). Z is an assumption. I assumed a 1.6 mm PCB and a terminal block, header and capacitor height of about 10 mm above the board, and I ignored any header pin length below the board. Mounting hole positions and diameters are estimated from pixel scaling of the top-view photo (about 0.0635 mm per pixel) with the origin at the board center. Both holes are assumed to be about 2.3 mm in diameter. The holes are assumed to be through-holes. The PCB is modeled at z = -6 to -4.4 mm. The many small header and castellated pad holes are not listed. No other features are inferred.
